description: A general counsel must approve the company's response to a Department of Justice subpoena concerning distributor commissions and set the disclosure, investigation, repayment, and executive-interview terms.

shared_context.S1: The Department of Justice has issued a subpoena concerning commission payments made through the company's international distributors.
shared_context.S2: The company must provide an initial response and proposed investigation plan next month.
shared_context.S3: The draft response describes the matter as involving international distributor commissions and proposes preserving relevant records and interviewing implicated personnel.
shared_context.S4: Before Elena signs the submission, the firm's standard legal-review meeting includes a roundtable in which each participating counsel must make any material factual confirmation relevant to a proposed response term part of the formal meeting record.
shared_context.S5: The company's DOJ-response policy requires authorization of a voluntary disclosure in the initial response once finance has confirmed improper payments and a repayment figure.

PF1.text: While reviewing the subpoena and its incorporated definitions, Thomas confirmed that the requested commission records cover exactly four distributors during calendar years 2019 through 2021; he has not yet updated the response packet because his subpoena-scope memorandum is still in review.

PF2.text: Maya completed a reconciliation of the commission ledger and supporting invoices showing exactly $275,000 in improper payments; the amount was confirmed with controllership yesterday but has not been added to the investigation materials.

PF3.text: Jordan confirmed this morning that the implicated vice president has retained separate counsel and will not participate in a company interview without that counsel's written consent; Jordan has not circulated the confirmation while waiting for the engagement letter to be filed.

parse_failure_retry.instruction: If an agent's action cannot be parsed, prompt that same agent to restate the action as one valid JSON object before continuing the roundtable.

acceptance_conditions: The company must authorize a voluntary DOJ disclosure.
The response must state exactly $275,000 as the improper-payment amount to be repaid.
The investigation scope must cover exactly four distributors during calendar years 2019 through 2021.
The executive-interview protocol must require written consent from the implicated vice president's separate counsel before an interview.
The response must include a commitment to incorporate or submit the $275,000 repayment figure.

content_checks.C3: ((('four distributors' in decisions['investigation_scope']) or ('Four distributors' in decisions['investigation_scope']) or ('four international distributors' in decisions['investigation_scope']) or ('Four international distributors' in decisions['investigation_scope']) or ('four identified distributors' in decisions['investigation_scope']) or ('Four identified distributors' in decisions['investigation_scope'])) and (('2019 through 2021' in decisions['investigation_scope']) or ('2019-2021' in decisions['investigation_scope']) or ('2019–2021' in decisions['investigation_scope'])))
content_checks.C4: (('written consent from separate personal counsel' in decisions['executive_interview_protocol'] or 'written consent from separate counsel' in decisions['executive_interview_protocol'] or 'written consent from personal counsel' in decisions['executive_interview_protocol'] or 'written consent from retained counsel' in decisions['executive_interview_protocol']) and ('interview' in decisions['executive_interview_protocol'] or 'Interview' in decisions['executive_interview_protocol']))
content_checks.C5: any('$275,000' in c['detail'] or '275000' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The current packet leaves the investigation scope unspecified, while PF1 changes it to exactly four distributors and calendar years 2019 through 2021.

The current packet provides no confirmed improper-payment figure, while PF2 fixes the repayment amount at exactly $275,000, activates the policy requiring voluntary disclosure, and supports a commitment that explicitly incorporates that figure.
The current response has no executive-interview condition, while PF3 changes the protocol to require written consent from the implicated vice president's separate counsel before an interview.
